newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville readies for higher hydropower dam flows.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville readies for higher hydropower dam flows.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) expects warmer Pacific Northwest weather and rain this week to reduce regional power demand and raise the volume of water flowing into hydroelectric projects.

"Last week the weather was unseasonally cold and there has been almost continuous precipitation in the (Columbia River) basin since the end of February," said Bill Berry, power operations specialist at BPA.
But he noted spikes in runoff are not that unusual for this time of year, and weather conditions remain uncertain.

Weather Services Corp forecast temperatures in the Pacific Northwest as much as 15 degrees F above normal through the end of the week, but the six to 10-day outlook was for temperatures to drop back to normal or slightly below normal.
Precipitation in the region was expected to continue through Thursday, but a high pressure system was seen ushering in drier conditions for the weekend.

In the worst case, heavy flows could trigger flood stage operations for the Northwest's hydroelectric dam system, and flows would be curtailed at upstream projects in order to minimize the amount of water flowing into the Portland area.
"Our initial concern will be the volume of lower elevation snow," Berry said.
He noted that volumes on the Snake River are already running fairly high and work is still underway at several hydro projects on equipment related to fish migration.
"The trouble is we can't get any more (power generating) capacity. We are already running at capacity for on-peak hours," Berry said.
Bonneville has dropped next-day prices for firm power during peak demand hours by $2.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) over the past week.
For Thursday, BPA offered 300 MW of peak firm power at $13.50 per MWh for Northwest sales and $14.50 for California-Oregon and Nevada-Oregon deliveries.
